items.title: Gaming su Mac, intervista allo sviluppatore che sta facendo quello che avrebbe dovuto fare Apple anni fa
items.summary: Uno sviluppatore, aiutato da ChatGPT Astra, sta portando su Mac, a colpi di un gioco al giorno, i migliori titoli Windows, con prestazioni ottime e stabilità notevole. Dimostrando che forse la strada scelta da Apple non è la più adatta in questi tempi. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il rapporto tra Apple e il gaming può essere riassunto con un episodio: alla WWDC 2025, ormai un anno fa, gli sviluppatori di CD Projekt RED con il loro Cyberpunk 2077 sono stati presi come testimonial di quanto fosse facile portare un gioco su Mac, e il loro titolo di punta è stato usato per mostrare le nuove funzionalità di Metal 4, come MetalFX Frame Interpolation, per generare fotogrammi intermedi e aumentare la fluidità, e MetalFX Denoising, per ridurre il rumore del ray tracing e consentire di spingersi verso impostazioni grafiche più elevate. Apple ci ha mostrato effettivamente Cyberpunk girare a 60 fps su un MacBook Air M4 grazie alla Frame Interpolation, e con il ray tracing alle impostazioni Ultra su un MacBook Pro con M4 Max, dicendo che l'update sarebbe uscito nell'autunno del 2025 insieme a macOS 26.

Oggi, a ottobre 2026, quella promessa non è ancora stata mantenuta e non è dato sapere se la tanto attesa patch arriverà mai .

A maggio 2026 Apple descriveva ancora Cyberpunk come un titolo che sfrutta Frame Interpolation e Denoising, mentre il gioco continua a usare la frame interpolation di AMD, con scarsi risultati.

Apple in questi anni ha ribadito più volte che la sua strategia gaming è costruita attorno a un principio cardine: i giochi su Mac devono arrivare "nativi", ovvero sviluppati con le tecnologie Apple. Ha seguito questa strada perché nel software è sempre stata abituata a veder rispondere tutti gli sviluppatori quando li ha chiamati a raccolta, per un cambio di architettura o per un nuovo prodotto: si sono sempre adattati in tempo record. Questa volta non ha però considerato un aspetto: il mondo dei giochi risponde ad altre logiche e si muove velocemente soprattutto se a chiamare sono altre aziende, Sony, NVIDIA, Microsoft.

Per quanto oggi la situazione sui nuovi titoli sia migliorata (alcuni giochi recenti sono usciti già in versione multipiattaforma), è evidente che non esiste proprio la possibilità che le software house rimettano mano a giochi già usciti, come ha fatto CD Projekt RED, probabilmente di fronte a un grosso incentivo economico, per rivederli in versione Mac nativa. Anche con l'IA che fa parte del lavoro sarebbe comunque un impegno troppo grande per aziende che navigano in un mercato in forte crisi, come dimostra la recente riorganizzazione di Microsoft.

La soluzione Apple ce l'avrebbe in casa, e non è una, sono tante. Tutti gli strumenti che in questi anni ha creato per aiutare a convertire un gioco: dal Game Porting Toolkit, pensato per analizzare e far girare su Mac i giochi Windows prima ancora di affrontare il porting vero e proprio, al Metal Shader Converter, che traduce gli shader DirectX per l'esecuzione su Metal. Ci sono poi MetalFX, con upscaling, frame interpolation e denoising, Metal-cpp per portare nei motori C++ le API grafiche di Apple e strumenti di profiling come Metal HUD, che permettono di individuare con precisione i colli di bottiglia del rendering.

Eppure, paradossalmente, mentre Apple continua a costruire strumenti sempre più sofisticati per convincere gli sviluppatori a fare porting nativi, c'è chi ha scelto di prendere la questione da un'altra angolazione: se il problema è che i giochi Windows non arrivano su Mac, perché non trovare un modo per farli girare bene così come sono?

Ci prova da qualche anno CrossOver, con un approccio però universale: un unico strumento che riesce a far girare più o meno bene il maggior numero possibile di giochi. Alcuni vanno bene, altri zoppicano, ma è un po' quello che succede con ogni strumento che emula o trascrive un'architettura: è impossibile trovare una chiave di ottimizzazione comune.

C'è invece chi ha preso una strada diversa, partendo da una sua esigenza personale: far girare Age of Empires IV su Mac con la miglior resa possibile, anche a costo di modificare gli strumenti in modi che possono penalizzare le prestazioni di altri giochi.

Così nasce GameToMac , progetto amatoriale di Marc Ibrahim che ha avuto così tanto successo da spingerlo a lavorarci a tempo pieno e a trasformarlo in un prodotto commerciale, anche se con un prezzo tutto sommato molto basso, circa 20 euro all'anno.

GameToMac ha un obiettivo preciso: dare un'applicazione plug & play che permetta di giocare a una selezione di titoli Windows senza dover armeggiare con Wine, prefix e script. È comparso in alpha ai primi di settembre e da allora la libreria è cresciuta in fretta: oggi sono indicati 20 titoli, dagli strategici di Microsoft/Relic (Age of Empires II, III e IV, Age of Mythology: Retold, Company of Heroes 3) agli action RPG (Elden Ring, Diablo IV, Path of Exile 2, Hogwarts Legacy, Skyrim Special Edition), fino ai più recenti GTA V Enhanced e Red Dead Redemption 2 in modalità storia ; l'online resta impossibile a causa degli anticheat.

I giochi aumentano al ritmo di uno al giorno, e l'arrivo di The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt in edizione remastered a un solo giorno dal rilascio su PC fa capire che l'intenzione è guardare ai titoli più recenti, rendendoli compatibili in poche ore. Rispetto a CrossOver, che fa girare un'ampia gamma di software Windows, GameToMac è solo una libreria selezionata, con ottimizzazioni e fix su misura per ciascun titolo.

Abbiamo chiesto al creatore, Marc Ibrahim, cosa succede quando si preme "Play" su GameToMac per far partire un singolo gioco. " GameToMac prepara le impostazioni e le correzioni di compatibilità per quel gioco, poi lo avvia tramite il suo launcher, di solito Steam. Gestisce la configurazione dietro le quinte, così puoi entrare direttamente nel gioco " ci dice, spiegando che sotto il cofano c'è Wine, ma non quello standard: " GameToMac usa un runtime Wine 11 modificato, con correzioni e ottimizzazioni aggiuntive per i giochi supportati. Si basa sul lavoro della community di Wine ".

La scelta architetturale più interessante di GameToMac è l'isolamento. " Ogni gioco ha il suo ambiente, con le sue impostazioni e le sue correzioni. Questo mi permette di ottimizzare un gioco senza cambiare la configurazione degli altri " spiega Ibrahim, confermando quello che chiunque lo abbia provato ha sicuramente notato. " Ogni gioco Steam ha un'installazione Windows di Steam separata all'interno del proprio ambiente. Continui a usare il tuo normale account Steam e i giochi che già possiedi, ma ogni gioco ha il suo Steam all'interno del quale è installato il singolo titolo ".

Sul fronte grafico, per passare da DirectX a Metal in tempo reale si usa il componente creato da Apple legato al Game Porting Toolkit. " Attualmente GameToMac usa D3DMetal 3.0. Alcuni giochi usano altri livelli grafici, a seconda di ciò che funziona meglio per quel titolo. L'app GameToMac è ovviamente nativa ARM64, ma oggi sia Wine sia D3DMetal girano tramite Rosetta. Rosetta non sarà più utilizzabile con la prossima versione di macOS, quindi sto iniziando a sperimentare con Wine ARM64 e FEX, con l'obiettivo di rendere in futuro GameToMac indipendente da Rosetta ".

Ancora più curioso è il motivo per cui i giochi girano davvero bene, senza problemi di prestazioni e con una stabilità notevole. " A volte è una semplice questione di configurazione, ma altri fix vanno più in profondità, dentro Wine o nel livello grafico. Una parte importante è identificare tutto il lavoro svolto dagli strumenti che viene ripetuto inutilmente, causando il crollo delle prestazioni, e metterlo in cache, che si tratti di codice generato, pipeline grafiche o informazioni richieste di frequente. Il fix che applico è specifico per ogni gioco, perché è frutto dell'analisi di dove quel gioco sta perdendo tempo e quindi prestazioni ".

Ci porta l'esempio di Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition. " Selezionare le unità con la grafica migliorata attiva causava un enorme calo di prestazioni. Ho scoperto che lo stesso controllo sui contenuti veniva ripetuto migliaia di volte al secondo, cosa che rendeva il gioco ingiocabile. Mettere in cache il risultato per pochi millisecondi ha eliminato gran parte di quel sovraccarico e sul mio Mac di test si è passati da circa 13 FPS a 120 FPS stabili. "

Per Age of Empires IV il problema era di natura diversa, ma il principio è lo stesso: evitare di rifare lavoro già fatto. " Molto tempo veniva speso a gestire eccezioni ripetute e a ritradurre codice generato. Con l'aiuto dell'IA ho modificato la gestione delle eccezioni di Wine e aggiunto una cache del codice, così che Rosetta potesse riutilizzare il proprio lavoro. Lato prestazioni c'è stato un salto enorme ".

ChatGPT Astra è stata fondamentale: " L'IA fa una parte sostanziale della scrittura del codice e dell'indagine. Io la guido, suggerisco idee e possibili correzioni e decido la direzione da prendere. Provo anche i giochi e riporto indietro ciò che succede davvero. È un continuo avanti e indietro tra idee, codice e gameplay reale" . Un debugging assistito: l'IA analizza i log di Wine e il livello grafico alla ricerca dei punti in cui si perde tempo, lo sviluppatore decide che strada prendere e verifica in gioco che il fix regga.

Non è ancora un PC: non ha la compatibilità di una macchina Windows o di una console, e non è pensabile che una soluzione come GameToMac possa magicamente risolvere il problema del gaming su Mac . Ma dimostra una cosa che forse Apple dovrebbe prendere più seriamente: non sempre è necessario chiedere agli sviluppatori di ricostruire un gioco per una piattaforma, quando si può rendere la piattaforma capace di eseguire ciò che già esiste.

items.title: Show HN: Minigraf – An embedded, bi-temporal graph database in Rust
items.summary: A successor project to my previous attempt at building a temporal graph database ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=23455516 ). This one builds on its predecessor's concept, but drops the dependency on another database to provide the storage, transaction and query engines. Minigraf is self-contained, packaged as a library crate, embeds into your application, and supports full bi-temporality. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49963394 Points: 10 # Comments: 1
items.content:
Embedded graph memory for AI agents, mobile apps, and the browser — the SQLite of bi-temporal graph databases

A tiny, self-contained graph database with Datalog queries and bi-temporal time travel . Think SQLite, but for connected data with full history.

Watch time travel in the visualizer → Scrub transaction time and valid time, and see the graph change.

Minigraf is a single-file embedded graph database that lets you:

Status : See ROADMAP.md for planned work and current direction.

Datalog is fundamentally better for graphs than SQL-like languages:

Requires Rust 1.89 or newer (the minimum supported Rust version, set in Cargo.toml ).

Bugs present in the current release, with affected versions, workarounds and fix versions, are listed in the pinned Known issues in the current release issue. The most important one on v2.x:

v2.x gets data-integrity and security fixes for 12 months after v3.0.0 ships. See the support policy .

See a working implementation of temporal reasoning with Minigraf at github.com/adityamukho/temporal_reasoning — an AI agent that uses Minigraf's bi-temporal model to store, correct, and audit beliefs.

The time travel visualizer runs Minigraf in your browser and draws its history. Step through transactions, move the valid-time cursor, and see each fact version on a bitemporal map. It opens .graph files too. For example, see a salary that was recorded wrong and then corrected .

See the Datalog Reference wiki page for the complete syntax.

Tier 1 bindings are fully tested and released at the same time as every core release. Tier 2 bindings are built and smoke-tested, released on a best-effort schedule, and experimental. A binding moves to Tier 1 when real users need it. Tier 1 operating systems and filesystems are Linux (ext4, xfs), macOS (APFS) and Windows (NTFS) on local disk; NFSv4 is supported with caveats, and NFSv3 nolock is unsupported for multiple writers. Details: support tiers .

Embedded graph memory for agents, mobile, and the browser — SQLite's simplicity + Datomic's temporal model.

See the Comparison wiki page for detailed analysis including temporal vs. time-series databases.

Store what an agent believes, retract and correct without losing history, and replay past states to audit decisions. Every fact carries both transaction time (when it was recorded) and valid time (when it was true), so you can reconstruct the exact knowledge state at the moment of any past decision.

Pairs well with vector stores (GraphRAG pattern): the vector store answers "what is similar?"; Minigraf answers "what are the relationships, who recorded them, and what did we believe at time T?"

See it in the visualizer: what an agent believed when it made a recommendation , and the correction that followed (press → to step forward).

Offline-first storage with retroactive corrections — the bi-temporal model lets you correct a mis-entered value while preserving the original record ( see a correction in the visualizer ). Native Kotlin and Swift bindings ship as an Android .aar (Maven Central) and an iOS .xcframework (Swift Package Manager) via UniFFI . No Rust required.

See the Mobile Integration wiki section for full setup and usage docs (Gradle config, SPM integration, error handling, threading).

Published as @minigraf/browser on npm (IndexedDB-backed, wasm-pack ). WASI build ( wasm32-wasip1 ) available as @minigraf/wasi on npm and as a GitHub Releases artifact (Wasmtime / Wasmer). See the Use Cases wiki . The playground and the time travel visualizer are both built on @minigraf/browser .

Language bindings ship as minigraf on PyPI, minigraf on npm (Node.js native addon), io.github.adityamukho:minigraf-jvm on Maven Central, and a C header + prebuilt shared library on GitHub Releases. See the Use Cases wiki .

See BENCHMARKS.md for the current reproducible local snapshot and benchmark commands. | Point query at 1M facts | 4.3–4.5 s (selective B+tree lookup for bounded patterns; O(N) for full-attribute scans) | | Open time at 1M facts | 1.31 s (2.4× faster than v5 — indexes no longer loaded into RAM) | | Peak heap at 1M facts | 1.05 GB (~21% less than v5 — indexes paged in on demand) |

File-backed databases enforce a maximum fact size of 4 080 serialised bytes per fact. In-memory databases have no limit.

Durability tuning: every write is fsync 'd immediately by default ( SyncMode::Full ). Bulk loaders/migrations that can safely re-run from a checkpoint watermark on failure can trade that for throughput with OpenOptions::new().synchronous(SyncMode::Normal) — checkpoint() still fsyncs unconditionally in both modes. See the Performance Tuning wiki page for the full tradeoff and the write-batching pattern that pairs with it.

This is a solo-maintained project with a long-term vision. Read PHILOSOPHY.md and ROADMAP.md before proposing features.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup, code standards, and the PR process.

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

items.title: Mold Linker Version 3.0.0 Release – Rewritten in Rust
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/rui314/mold/releases/tag/v3.0.0 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49963385 Points: 32 # Comments: 12
items.content:
mold 3.0.0 is a new major release of the high-speed linker. As we announced in the 2.42.1 release notes , we have rewritten mold from C++ to Rust, and this is the first release of the Rust version. 2.42.1 is the last release of the C++ version. The goal of mold 3.x is to close the remaining compatibility gaps with GNU ld, particularly in linker script support, and to pave the way for mold to be adopted as the default linker in Linux distributions.

mold 3.0 is meant to be a drop-in replacement for 2.42.1. It accepts the same command-line options, supports the same target architectures, and produces the same output except for the bug fixes listed below. Linking performance remains on par with 2.42.1. We verified compatibility by running the test suite on every supported target, comparing linker output across a broad range of real-world workloads and option combinations, and building all Gentoo packages. We found no regressions.

The move to Rust also makes mold safer with corrupted input files. The C++ version could read memory out of bounds on such input and crash with a segmentation fault. In mold 3.0, those reads are bounds-checked, so mold stops with a panic at the faulty access instead.

If you build mold yourself, note that the build system has changed. See "Build Changes" below.

mold is now built with Cargo instead of CMake. It requires Rust 1.95 or later and a C compiler. Run cargo build --release to build mold and ./install-mold.sh to install it; the install script accepts PREFIX and DESTDIR . The CMake options have been removed.

If you install mold's libraries into a directory other than $PREFIX/lib , such as /usr/lib64 , set the MOLD_LIBDIR environment variable to that directory both when building and when installing mold, so that mold -run can find mold-wrapper.so .

mold no longer depends on oneTBB . It statically links mimalloc 3.5.3 as before; build with --features system-allocator to use the system's malloc instead. mold links the system's zlib if available and includes zstd and BLAKE3; set ZSTD_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1 to link the system's zstd. ( 56ee0f8 )

The MOLD_TARGETS CMake variable has been replaced with Cargo features. As before, distributions should build mold for all targets.

The test suite now runs with cargo test instead of ctest . install-build-deps.sh has been replaced with install-test-deps.sh , which you need only to run the tests.

Fixed a crash when creating a statically-linked executable with a version script or --default-symver . ( f10b0c4 )

Fixed a crash or a corrupted output when the output file is also an input file, as in mold -r -o foo.o foo.o bar.o . ( d2b88ab )

--gc-sections no longer removes the functions given by --init and --fini . ( c9e4cc4 )

Common symbols of the same name with different sizes now get the largest size and the strictest alignment, as in GNU ld and lld. ( d5781d5 )

--icf=safe no longer folds functions exported from a shared library, and --icf=all no longer crashes with --emit-relocs . ( ceab12c , 3dcd1df )

A versioned reference such as foo@VER in a shared library no longer pulls in an archive member that defines an unversioned foo . ( #1657 ) ( 44bfa2a )

Fixed several cases of nondeterministic output, in --dependency-file , --repro , -r with many COMDAT groups of the same name, and some dynamic relocations. ( 5164561 , 6d33903 , 51e23d4 , 696ed71 )

Fixed several -r bugs: C++ exceptions broke in code from the second and later input files; -x , -X and -s removed symbols that relocations referred to; --gc-sections dropped data that relocations referred to; sh_link of SHF_LINK_ORDER sections such as .ARM.exidx was not set; and mold crashed with --strip-debug and DWARF type units. ( 0e41bb9 , 3717460 , b2c3d1d , 9aacb62 , a247ca2 , e41ed90 )

GOT-relative relocations such as R_X86_64_GOTOFF64 , and R_ARM_REL32 , against symbols defined in shared libraries silently got wrong addresses. They are now handled correctly or reported as errors. ( #1668 ) ( 659780e , 7fe68bf )

Errors for PC-relative relocations that can't be used in position-independent output now explain the cause and how to fix it. ( 39e6a01 , 17b7b85 )

The following now cause errors instead of a broken output or a crash: --defsym aliasing a symbol defined in a shared library, an undefined non-weak hidden symbol in a shared library or with --unresolved-symbols=ignore-all , a --defsym value that doesn't fit in 64 bits, an allocated section that is also compressed, and --strip-all with --emit-relocs . ( 56b862b , b3566fa , e3a89f2 , a980054 , 8233a75 )

--noinhibit-exec no longer crashes on references to symbols in discarded COMDAT groups. ( 8f17166 , 80baa5d )

Options starting with a single dash are now read as GNU ld reads them. For example, -entry=main was read as -e ntry=main . ( #1671 , #1670 ) ( 830a860 )

--dynamic-list-data , --lto-pseudo-probe-for-profiling and --thinlto-index-only no longer consume the next argument, and --no-color-diagnostics is now accepted. ( 2ca893e , 04b493e )

If a version script lists a symbol in more than one version node, the first one now takes precedence, as in GNU ld and lld. ( b7048f5 )

Fixed relative paths with -C , --chroot and --repro . ( e3bc349 , 04e7dd8 , a368d22 )

mold no longer reserves 8 GiB of virtual address space at startup, so it works under ulimit -v . ( cc69390 , b18be91 )

MOLD_JOBS now works if XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is an empty string. ( 8a360ff )

Files created by --separate-debug-file no longer contain a .gnu_debuglink section. ( #1656 ) ( b56649e )

mold no longer creates the meaningless __start_EHDR , __stop_EHDR , __start_PHDR and __stop_PHDR symbols. ( 0ee71d3 )

[AArch64][PPC32][ARM32] Fixed calls to static functions in other sections through range extension thunks, which jumped to wrong addresses in large programs such as the ARM64 debug build of Chromium. ( 4165d0e , 9b91621 )

[AArch64] Added support for more relocation types, such as R_AARCH64_TSTBR14 and R_AARCH64_GOT_LD_PREL19 . ( 96d0282 , a4b64d8 )

[ARM32] Added support for more relocation types, such as R_ARM_ALU_PC_G0 and R_ARM_THM_PC12 , and fixed -r output for big-endian ARM. ( c0f9cd6 , 4c9aad3 , 4c26f16 )

[ARM32][i386] -r no longer corrupts instructions referred to by some branch and TLS relocations. ( 1b17bdf )

[RISC-V][LoongArch] Fixed calls to functions folded by --icf=all when relaxation shrinks them, and R_RISCV_64 and R_LARCH_64 relocations in 32-bit objects. ( 52febe9 , 5b22233 )

[RISC-V] Fixed TLSDESC with object files created by Clang 18, --emit-relocs with TLSDESC relaxation, the EF_RISCV_TSO flag, R_RISCV_ALIGN in -r output, and overflow checks for 32-bit PC-relative relocations. ( fdf8422 , 7c8b805 , 6b60f75 , 4ba7792 , 85d55f3 )

[LoongArch] Added support for TLSDESC in the extreme code model, and fixed wrong values of *64_PC_HI12 relocations and spurious overflow errors for TLS relocations. ( a36a161 , 8133938 , 13e6cc0 )

[PPC32][m68k] A GOT too large for the 16-bit offsets that -fpic code uses is now reported as an error instead of being silently truncated. ( acc8854 , 614e2a0 )

[PPC64] Fixed IFUNC calls in statically-linked executables and @got references in hand-written assembly, and mold now synthesizes the _savegpr0_* family of functions for PPC64V1 as well. ( d3b2a74 , b34a308 , efda2fc )

[SH4] Fixed a crash when calling a function that returns a structure through the PLT, and C++ exceptions in programs linked from -r output. ( d9cf1f0 , 92161dd )

[SPARC64] Fixed branch instructions using R_SPARC_WDISP16 , and R_SPARC_OLO10 in -r output. ( 6df3fd2 , 269fbb9 )

items.title: Europe's new robotics unicorn: Germany's RobCo hits $1B valuation
items.summary: Article URL: https://techfundingnews.com/europes-new-robotics-unicorn-germanys-robco-hits-1b-valuation/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49963366 Points: 264 # Comments: 226
items.content:
RobCo has surpassed a $1 billion valuation through a secondary share sale that allows long-standing employees to realise part of the value they helped create, while bringing new investment into the Munich-founded autonomous robotics company.

The transaction combines new investment into the business with a secondary share sale that gives long-standing employees the opportunity to realise part of the value they have helped create since RobCo’s founding.

Existing investors Sequoia, Lightspeed, Greenfield, Kindred, Lingotto and Promus Ventures participated alongside new investors including Cherry Ventures and European Tech Collective, a group of founders behind some of Europe’s most successful technology companies.

This follows RobCo’s $100 million Series C announced in January 2026 , co-led by Lightspeed and Lingotto, to expand its Physical AI platform and US operations.

“This is an important moment for RobCo, and I cannot think of a better way to mark it than by giving some of the people who built this company the opportunity to realize part of the value they created,” said Roman Hölzl , Co-founder and CEO of RobCo. “There was strong demand to invest in RobCo, so we used that moment to strengthen the company.”

RobCo was founded in 2020 by Roman Hölzl, Paul Maroldt , and Constantin Dresel , RobCo is building autonomous industrial robotics around a Robotics-as-a-Service model, allowing manufacturers to deploy automation without significant upfront investment.

At the centre of the company’s next phase is Alfie, a robot designed to combine perception, reasoning and execution for high-mix, unstructured and safety-critical industrial work.

RobCo plans to commercially launch Alfie at RobCoN, its first annual summit, in Munich on March 4, 2027.

The company is already expanding rapidly in the US, its fastest-growing market. Customer operations now span more than a dozen states, supported by manufacturing and assembly operations in Austin, Texas, and a laboratory in San Francisco. Hölzl has also relocated to the US to lead the expansion.

The opportunity is expanding alongside RobCo’s ambitions. The International Federation of Robotics says factories worldwide installed 603,000 industrial robots in 2025, up 11% , while the global operational stock reached 5.079 million robots, up 9%. The IFR expects installations to rise another 9% to 655,000 units in 2026.

RobCo faces increasingly well-funded rivals targeting different parts of industrial automation.

Standard Bots raised $200 million in Series C funding in June 2026 at a $1 billion valuation, co-led by General Catalyst and RoboStrategy, to scale AI-powered industrial robots across US factories.

Walden Robotics emerged from stealth in July with $300 million in seed funding at a $1.1 billion valuation, backed by Toyota and Deviation Capital, with robots already working inside Toyota factories.

Meanwhile, UK-based Dexory raised $165 million in its latest funding round , including a $100 million Series C, to scale autonomous robots and AI-powered warehouse intelligence globally.

RobCo’s ambition goes beyond selling another industrial robot. By combining autonomous hardware, AI-driven software and Robotics-as-a-Service, it wants factories to deploy machines that can adapt to changing environments rather than remain locked into narrowly defined tasks.

“RobCo is building for a future in which AI doesn’t just reason and generate, but acts in the physical world. The progress the company has made over the past few years is impressive, but we believe this is still the beginning”, added Luciana Lixandru , Partner at Sequoia Capital.

With its valuation now above $1 billion, its US expansion accelerating and Alfie approaching commercial launch, RobCo is betting that the next generation of factory automation will be defined not simply by robots, but by machines capable of understanding and acting in the physical world.

items.title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost
items.summary: The star reveals why he is "very selective" about releasing music - and shares his future collab hopes.
items.content:
Can you find success as an Indian artist, outside of the Bollywood machine, while making music that feels like you?

Well according to Anuv Jain it's possible - and you can even create something "beautiful".

The singer-songwriter's soft vocals have gained hundreds of millions of views on YouTube - not an easy feat as an independent artist in India's music scene.

BBC Newsbeat met Jain as he prepared for the final shows on the European leg of his first world tour to find out why he's taking his time and "hoping for the best".

"It's not about the numbers," Jain tells us backstage, ahead of his sold-out performance at London's Roundhouse.

Jain is from Ludhiana in the Punjab region of India and began singing as a teenager.

His tracks have since racked up hundreds of millions of views on YouTube with their emotional storylines about relationships and heartbreak.

Jain primarily sings in Hindi, with his pieces often exploring deep emotions like love and longing.

Fans talk about feeling like his music soundtracks their lives , external and is personal to them.

His accessible style has attracted 3.9 million followers on Instagram and more than 20 million monthly listeners on Spotify.

When writing music, he says, he imagines how someone listening in the car, going for a run or sitting alone at night would feel hearing the song.

"I just try to make a good song and something that I would like to listen to, something my mum, my sister and my wife would like to listen to," he says.

"For some reason, the taste that we have in music is gentle enough that when we put it out there, there are millions of people who are wanting to consume all of this."

Jain has attracted a sizeable fanbase without the backing of Bollywood, which has traditionally dominated the Indian music industry with opportunities and significant funding for artists.

He's one of a growing number of independent musicians offering something different to the rollicking film scores and dramatic ballads that are synonymous with the country's movie industry.

Jain describes artists like him as existing in an "alternate space".

"We release music ourselves and hope for the best," he says.

Jo Tum Mere Ho and Afsos, Jain's track with AP Dhillon, both reached number one on the Asian Music Charts, but the singer says there's no recipe to his success.

Jain says he's "very selective" about the music he releases, only putting out one song a year until recently.

But he plans to change that - and insists he has new songs coming "very soon".

"They're done and I think they're beautiful songs so technically you might have more music this year," he says.

"It's not like it's gonna be just one release, let's see how it works out."

The singer explains that seeing a project through is key - which might be why he limits what he puts out.

"There are no projects like right now for me that are half or that I haven't completed them yet.

"When I start a project, I always finish it. I mean, I might have ideas, but as soon as I start writing, I finish it."

Simplicity seems to do the trick, with certain passages , external of Jain's songs, like Arz Kiya Hai, becoming hugely popular among his fanbase and going viral on TikTok and Instagram.

There have been high-profile collaborations between some of western music and Indian music's biggest names in recent years.

Jain says he'd be open to working with bigger stars, but only if his own identity can be preserved and things are done "the right way".

"The storytelling cannot get diluted just because there's a bigger name attached," he says.

However, Jain does admit he could see himself joining forces with former One Direction star Zayn Malik, who's enjoyed success in both the Official Singles Chart and Official Asian Music Chart.

"He would be somebody who would definitely work very well with the kind of music that I make," says Jain.

Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

items.title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain
items.summary: US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded for their work.
items.content:
US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work in the field of optogenetics.

Their research has helped scientists learn more about the inner workings of the brain, to better understand how the human mind works.

The Nobel Committee , external praised the trio for laying the foundation of a new era in neuroscience by revealing how to switch on and off neural circuits behind "specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders".

In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method to try to restore sight in people with visual impairment .

"Optogenetics has fundamentally altered our understanding of the brain," the Nobel Assembly said.

"Every day brings new discoveries, helping to solve one of humanity's great mysteries: how our incredible brain works."

The winners said it was "absolutely wonderful" to get the award, and that it was an honour to share the accolade with friends.

The three men will also share the £900,000 (12 million Swedish kronor) prize money.

Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, explained: "Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of."

Before, the inner workings behind feelings, behaviours and bodily functions were more of a mystery to scientists.

Optogentics is a way to illuminate brain pathways, using a special protein borrowed from algae that scientists use to control cell electrical activity using light.

In the early 2000s, Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, the algal protein with unique properties.

Deisseroth worked out how to use this light controlled protein to switch on nerve cells in the brains of mice.

Researchers have since been able to study nerve cells and pathways in animals to see and discover more about what they do.

The Nobel Committee said: "Using light, researchers are now able to switch individual neural circuits on or off in the brain. They can bring memories to life, create feelings, drive behaviours and study the types of neurons that are involved in various psychiatric and neurological disorders."

That is providing important insights into how the nervous system interacts with various cells in other areas of the body, such as in the heart and gut, the committee added.

Researchers have also taken "the first steps" towards using optogenetics as a medical treatment, the committee explained.

In ongoing clinical trials, scientists have been working to restore vision in people who have become blind due to retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that destroys the eye's rods and cones.

By inserting a special protein in the damaged region of the eye, the patient regained some vision when wearing special glasses emitting light. This switched on the therapeutic algae proteins.

items.title: Ex Ilva, la Corte di Milano conferma il blocco degli altoforni
items.summary: Giudici respingono anche seconda istanza sospensiva. Udienza in Cassazione il 20 ottobre
items.content:
La Corte d'Appello di Milano ha confermato, per la seconda volta, il provvedimento con cui a luglio è stato disposto lo spegnimento degli altoforni dell'ex Ilva da mettere in atto entro fine ottobre. Il collegio di giudici, presieduto da Giuseppe Ondei, ha infatti respinto anche la seconda istanza di sospensiva presentata dai legali dell'ex Ilva in amministrazione straordinaria e di AdI spa, che avevano chiesto la sospensione della decisione sul blocco dell'area a caldo in vista dell'udienza della Cassazione, a cui hanno fatto ricorso, già fissata per il 20 ottobre.

" La salute vince ancora su un pregiudizio economico giudicato sempre più cedevole e pretestuoso". E' il commento dell'avvocato Ascanio Amenduni, legale dei cittadini di Taranto che hanno intentato la causa civile davanti ai giudici milanesi, sezione imprese, che ha portato al blocco dell'area a caldo dell'ex Ilva da mettere in atto entro fine ottobre. Oggi, infatti, la Corte d'Appello di Milano ha rigettato "i ricorsi proposti da Ilva Spa e da Acciaierie d'Italia Spa" in amministrazione straordinaria, con i quali era stata "chiesta la sospensione dell'efficacia esecutiva del decreto" della Corte dello scorso luglio.

Il 30 settembre, davanti ai giudici, si era tenuta la discussione delle parti. Anche il sostituto pg Angelo Renna aveva chiesto di respingere la nuova istanza di sospensiva, dopo quella rigettata già l'11 settembre. I legali della ex Ilva e di AdI, invece, avevano ribadito le loro ragioni, ossia il danno irreparabile - sostenevano - dovuto allo spegnimento e avevano chiesto tempo fino a dopo il giudizio della Cassazione, fissata per il 20 ottobre . Ascanio Amenduni, l'avvocato dei cittadini tarantini, invece, aveva spiegato che, essendo ora "l'impianto al minino", non c'era nemmeno alcun "pregiudizio irreparabile".

Secondo la Corte, come si legge nell'ordinanza di 12 pagine, "la fissazione dell'udienza" della Suprema Corte non cambia nulla, rispetto ai precedenti provvedimenti che hanno indicato la prevalenza del diritto alla salute , date le emissioni nocive degli impianti e la presenza di amianto. Non cambia nulla, si legge, "rispetto al passato in ordine alla tutela sostanziale degli interessi coinvolti" e la fissazione di quell'udienza è solo " meramente consequenziale alla presentazione dei ricorsi straordinari avanti alla Suprema Corte di Cassazione"

Il "pericolo" che consegue "all'eventuale 'spegnimento' degli altiforni" deve cedere "rispetto al preminente diritto alla salute nell'ottica del necessario bilanciamento dei contrapposti interessi". La tutela "del diritto alla salute", infatti, è "comunque prevalente, nel doveroso rispetto dell'interpretazione data in sede comunitaria, oltre che delle stesse previsioni costituzionali". Lo scrive la Corte d'Appello di Milano, sezione imprese (giudici Ondei-Del Vecchio-Cortelloni), nel provvedimento con cui ha respinto la seconda istanza di sospensiva dei legali dell'ex Ilva e di AdI, confermando di fatto il provvedimento di luglio sul blocco dell'area a caldo dello stabilimento siderurgico tarantino da mettere in atto entro il 28 ottobre.

"Basta alibi, il governo dia risposte. Siamo di fronte all'ennesima sentenza che, come tutte le altre, rispettiamo. Ma l'esigenza che questo rispetto venga riconosciuto alla città diviene contestualmente sempre più urgente". Lo afferma il sindaco di Taranto Piero Bitetti commentando la decisione della Corte d'Appello di Milano. " Gli alibi per chi deve assumersi delle responsabilità - aggiunge - vengono periodicamente meno e l'attesa verso i verdetti della magistratura comincia a non essere più sufficiente per rinviare le decisioni. La tutela della salute è ormai scolpita a caratteri nitidi nelle coscienze di tutti. Ora tocca al governo dire cosa intenda fare di Taranto, quali scelte di politica industriale vuole mettere in atto". Se, osserva ancora il primo cittadino, " stiamo assistendo all'epilogo della siderurgia in riva allo Ionio , da Roma ci attendiamo investimenti che sappiano valorizzare le alternative economiche. Ci aspettiamo che la città rivesta un ruolo centrale nel tavolo interministeriale che abbiamo chiesto e che, oggi, ci sembra improcrastinabile. Dovremmo tenerlo proprio a Taranto, affinché sia chiaro che le decisioni si prendono qui". "Non serve rimandare ancora, serve decidere", conclude Bitetti.

items.title: La nuova macchina Nescafé Dolce Gusto riconosce le capsule e sceglie automaticamente l’estrazione
items.summary: Il nuovo sistema arriva in due versioni, Caffè e Latte, con capsule a base carta compostabili. Prezzi da 89 euro ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
È arrivata una nuova macchina da caffè della linea Nescafé Dolce Gusto: si chiama NEO e fa vari salti in avanti rispetto alle macchine da caffè già sul mercato, le Original.

La novità principale è il riconoscimento automatico della bevanda inserita : la macchina identifica la capsula tramite un sistema ottico e regola di conseguenza temperatura, pressione, quantità d’acqua e tempi di estrazione.

La gamma include due modelli. NEO Caffè è rivolta principalmente a chi utilizza espresso, Americano e preparazioni più lunghe. NEO Latte aggiunge invece le funzioni dedicate, appunto, alle bevande con latte e la tecnologia AirFoam.

Al centro della piattaforma c’è SmartBrew 3-in-1, che gestisce tre differenti modalità di preparazione. Per l’espresso viene utilizzata un’estrazione ad alta pressione, fino a 15 bar; per l’Americano entra invece in funzione Top-Up, che aggiunge acqua calda a un espresso già estratto; mentre Slow-Brew utilizza un’erogazione più lenta, goccia a goccia, pensata per avvicinarsi al caffè filtro.

La versione NEO Latte aggiunge AirFoam, il sistema dedicato alla preparazione della schiuma per cappuccino e altre bevande a base latte. L’obiettivo è integrare queste preparazioni nello stesso flusso della macchina, senza richiedere una sequenza separata di passaggi.

Le macchine saranno commercializzate nelle versioni De’Longhi e Krups. NEO Caffè sarà disponibile nelle colorazioni nero, grigio scuro, grigio e grigio ghiaccio con un prezzo consigliato di 89 euro. NEO Latte arriverà in bianco, grigio e grigio ghiaccio a 109 euro.

Collegando la macchina all’app Nescafé Dolce Gusto è possibile modificare lunghezza e temperatura, salvare le proprie preferenze e ricevere notifiche relative alla manutenzione. Con le nuove macchine da caffè viene introdotto anche un nuovo formato di capsule.

Quelle dedicate al caffè sono realizzate con circa un grammo di carta proveniente da fornitori certificati FSC, un sottile rivestimento interno in biopolimero compostabile e una membrana superiore in cellulosa: sono certificate per il compostaggio sia domestico sia industriale e, una volta utilizzate, possono essere conferite nell’organico oppure in una compostiera domestica.

Invece le bustine utilizzate per le preparazioni a base latte sono a base carta e possono essere conferite nella raccolta differenziata.

Il lancio di NEO non comporterà comunque l’uscita di scena della gamma esistente: Nescafé Dolce Gusto continuerà a commercializzare anche le macchine e le capsule della famiglia Original.

items.title: SodaStream finalmente in sconto: tutti lo vogliono!
items.summary: Scopri il gasatore d’acqua SodaStream, ora disponibile in sconto su Amazon. Trasforma la tua acqua in frizzante e risparmia con questa offerta speciale ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il gasatore d’acqua SodaStream è la soluzione per chi desidera trasformare l'acqua naturale in acqua frizzante comodamente a casa propria: progettato per offrire un'esperienza di gasatura semplice e veloce, ti permette di godere di acqua frizzante in pochi secondi.

SodaStream include un cilindro di CO2 che consente di gasare fino a 60 litri di acqua. Questo significa che potrai godere di acqua frizzante per un lungo periodo senza dover sostituire frequentemente il cilindro. Inoltre, il prodotto viene fornito con due bottiglie da 1 litro e una bottiglia da 0,5 litri, tutte lavabili in lavastoviglie, per una maggiore praticità e igiene.

Il design moderno e compatto del gasatore si adatta perfettamente a qualsiasi cucina, mentre il suo utilizzo intuitivo lo rende accessibile a tutti: basta inserire una bottiglia nel dispositivo, premere un pulsante e in pochi secondi avrai acqua frizzante pronta da gustare.

SodaStream è disponibile ora in offerta Prime Anticipata al prezzo di 59,99 euro .

items.title: Legge elettorale: fiducia su 3 articoli, opposizione protesta. Tutte le tappe prima del voto finale
items.summary: L’ultimo atto del Melonellum è previsto, a scrutinio segreto, giovedì 8 ottobre con dichiarazioni in diretta tv
items.content:
Legge elettorale, è la settimana decisiva. Il governo, come preannunciato, oggi ha posto la questione di fiducia sui primi tre articoli della riforma, modificati, insieme all'articolo 8, al Senato. Protesta l’opposizione. "L'apposizione della fiducia è indegna" ed "esprimiamo il disagio più profondo per uno schiaffo a questo ramo del Parlamento", dice Federico Fornaro del Pd nell'Aula di Montecitorio. "Avete paura della democrazia e dei vostri parlamentari", le parole di Filiberto Zaratti di Avs. "Noi stiamo mettendo in soffitta la democrazia parlamentare", afferma Enrica Alifano del M5s. "Fermatevi, si può fare una normativa più ragionevole", l'appello di Riccardo Magi di Più Europa, che ha organizzato un flash mob davanti a palazzo Chigi e ha annunciato di aver scritto una lettera al presidente della Repubblica Sergio Mattarella per illustrargli le ragioni dello sciopero della fame che sta conducendo da sei giorni in protesta contro la riforma elettorale, "una legge antidemocratica, che fa diventare una minoranza nel Paese maggioranza schiacciante in Parlamento".

Sul fronte della maggioranza, il capogruppo di FdI al Senato, Lucio Malan ragiona invece sulla data del voto a Un giorno da pecora su Rai Radio 1: "La scadenza è cinque anni. Abbiamo votato a settembre, quindi si potrebbe rivotare a settembre. Il difetto per il voto a settembre è che hai poco tempo per la campagna elettorale, e poi c'è da fare la legge di Bilancio, che è molto delicata. Per cui potrebbe esserci l'esigenza di votare a maggio e potrebbe avere un senso votare insieme alle Comunali"

Intanto, ecco come si procederà da qui all'8 ottobre, quando alle 12.30 si terrà il voto finale sulla riforma a scrutinio segreto.

Il governo, con il ministro per i rapporti con il Parlamento, Luca Ciriani , ha posto la fiducia sui primi tre articoli della riforma della legge elettorale. La fiducia è posta sui testi modificati dal Senato: di conseguenza, gli emendamenti presentati dalle opposizioni non saranno esaminati. I primi due articoli disciplinano il nuovo sistema di elezione della Camera e sistema di elezione del Senato, ovvero il 'cuore' della riforma, un sistema proporzionale con premio di maggioranza a chi ottiene almeno il 42% dei voti in entrambi i rami del Parlamento. Nei primi due articoli si prevedono, in particolare, i capilista bloccati con la possibilità di dare fino a tre preferenze a partire dal secondo in lista e con l'alternanza di genere se l'elettore dà più di una preferenza e l'aumento della raccolta firme per i partiti non presenti in Parlamento, come da modifiche apportate durante l'esame al Senato. Il terzo articolo disciplina i nuovi collegi di Bolzano.

Come da regolamento della Camera la fiducia si vota con chiama per appello nominale dei deputati dopo 24 ore. I deputati voteranno quindi, non prima delle 14, la prima fiducia sull'articolo 1. Non ci sarà voto finale sull'articolo (ma solo voto finale sul provvedimento). Dalle 12 sono previste le dichiarazioni di voto sulla fiducia. Terminata la votazione della fiducia sull'articolo 1 (che dura approssimativamente un'ora e un quarto) intorno alle 15.30 si terranno le dichiarazioni di voto sulla fiducia posta (oggi) sull'articolo 2 e a seguire la chiama dei deputati.

Dalle 9 si terranno le dichiarazioni di voto sulla terza fiducia posta dal governo lunedì e poi, non prima delle 10.50, ci sarà la chiama per appello nominale dei deputati. A seguire, entro le 13.30 si terranno le dichiarazioni di voto e, a seguire, il voto sull'articolo 8. La modifica del Senato ha introdotto il voto fuorisede per i caregiver. Non è possibile chiedere il voto segreto (in quanto non riguarda direttamente il meccanismo di trasformazione di voti in seggi) e si tratta di una modifica e di un articolo sostenuti anche dalle opposizioni e votati all'unanimità. Al termine, e dopo il question time, dalle 16.15 si svolgerà l'esame degli ordini del giorno fino alle 20 e con eventuale prosecuzione notturne.

Dalle 10.30 gli interventi con dichiarazioni di voto finale in diretta tv e voto a scrutinio segreto alle 12.30 con diretta Rai.

items.summary: Article URL: https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-introducing-web-search-api/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49963171 Points: 185 # Comments: 97
items.content:
Web Search API is now available in beta. Web Search API lets your AI agents and applications search the Internet and ground their responses in live information, instead of guessing URLs or relying on a model's training cutoff.

At launch, you can choose between three search providers: Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup . All three support Zero Data Retention for requests made through Cloudflare, and all have committed to Cloudflare's verified bot crawling standards.

Web Search API runs through AI Gateway , so search requests appear in your gateway logs and are billed to your AI Gateway credits at each provider's list API price, with no additional markup. You can also bring your own provider API key.

items.title: Press Release: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49963094 Points: 107 # Comments: 25
items.content:
The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet has decided to award the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine jointly to:

KARL DEISSEROTH The Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University, USA

“for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”

The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 is awarded for optogenetics — a method that makes it possible to show how nerve cells shape memories, feelings and behaviours in the living brain. Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered a remarkable protein, channelrhodopsin, in a single-celled alga. Karl Deisseroth transformed the protein into a light-controlled switch for nerve cells. The laureates have laid the foundation of a new era in neuroscience.

The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 is awarded for optogenetics — a method that makes it possible to show how nerve cells shape memories, feelings and behaviours in the living brain. Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered a remarkable protein, channelrhodopsin, in a single-celled alga. Karl Deisseroth transformed the protein into a light-controlled switch for nerve cells. The Laureates have laid the foundation of a new era in neuroscience.

How the brain governs feelings, behaviours and bodily functions has long been a mystery. In the 20th century, researchers began to investigate which areas of the brain affect which functions, but the methods used meant they could not prove causal relationships. The image they developed of the brain was like a sketch map, full of question marks and unknowns. Now all this is changing.

“Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of,” says Per Svenningsson, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine.

It all began with Peter Hegemann’s curiosity. He wondered how Chlamydomonas , a single-celled alga, is able to swim towards a light source. In the early 2000s, he and Georg Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin, an algal protein with unique properties, found on the surface of the cell. When it is illuminated by blue light, a channel opens through the protein. Charged ions then flow into the cell, creating an electrical impulse. They found that regardless of which cell they put the protein in, those cells became light sensitive.

Karl Deisseroth introduced the gene for channel-rhodopsin into nerve cells from rats. By illuminating the cells with blue light, he was able to trigger a nerve signal. He published this breakthrough in 2005. Two years later, he made this light-controlled switch for nerve cells work in the brains of living mice.

This method for controlling nerve signals with light is now called optogenetics, and it has rapidly gained global impact. Using optogenetics, researchers have been able to reveal neural circuits governing specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders. In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method in attempts to restore sight in people with visual impairment.

Optogenetics has fundamentally altered our understanding of the brain. Every day brings new discoveries, helping to solve one of humanity’s great mysteries: how our incredible brain works.

items.title: Supporters of jailed ex-PM Imran Khan begin march in Pakistan
items.summary: Thousands have taken to the streets after talks between authorities and Khan's party ended in deadlock.
items.content:
Thousands of supporters of Pakistan's jailed ex-prime minister Imran Khan have begun a march from the country's north-west as they call for his release.

Concerns over the 74-year-old's health have grown louder in recent months. His family claims he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

The cricket star-turned-politician, who faces charges in more than 100 cases, was jailed for 17 years over corruption last year. Khan said all the cases against him are politically motivated.

Even behind bars, he remains a force in Pakistani politics, and demonstrations in his support have led to deadly violence and crackdowns in the past.

The march began on Sunday in Lakki Marwat, a city 275km (170 miles) from Islamabad, and was expected to resume on Monday after pausing for the night.

Originally scheduled for last week, it was postponed to allow for talks between the government and Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party but the talks ended in deadlock.

Khan, who faces charges ranging from leaking state secrets to selling state gifts, was first imprisoned in August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year.

Sohail Afridi, chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province which is governed by the PTI, expects the march to make its way to a town about 80km west of the capital Islamabad by Thursday.

"[By then] this movement will have reached every corner of the country and every square will have become a centre of activity," he said on Sunday, urging the people to "play an active role in the political process".

While the march organisers have not announced that they were heading for Islamabad, authorities have stacked up shipping containers to block key access routes to the capital.

The PTI said talks with government failed because authorities rejected the party's request for access to Khan so that its leaders could consult him on national and political issues.

The party also said it had demanded that Khan be given an immediate medical examination and treatment.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi meanwhile accused Afridi of "sabotaging" negotiations, saying the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government had backed out of earlier commitments on counter-terrorism issues, according to Pakistan's local media reports.

In August, Khan was briefly transferred from jail to a state-run hospital for medical examination and treatment following complaints about his deteriorating health. The doctors later deemed him "medically fit".

The intervention was the most significant relief Khan has received from the courts since he was imprisoned in 2023 on corruption charges, which he says were politically motivated.

Khan's family and the PTI, however, criticised the authorities for defying a court order that he be examined by physicians at a specific private hospital.

On 20 September, Khan's sister Aleema Khanum was arrested in the eastern city of Lahore.

The arrest order said Khanum had been mobilising people to "create law and order situations" and "raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the Government".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as the country's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things.

At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence.

Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging Khan to be given proper medical care.

items.title: Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests
items.summary: Sánchez says Spain will head to the polls on 29 November after recent defeats on measures aimed at addressing the country's housing crisis.
items.content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early election for 29 November after recent defeats on legislation aimed at addressing the country's housing crisis.

Speculation about a snap election had been building over the weekend after parliament rejected two decree laws put forward by the minority government to protect tenants in the rental market.

The eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home after she was unable to afford a sharp rent rise has sparked nationwide protests and increased pressure for housing reform.

In a televised address on Monday, Sánchez said that to push reforms through he needed "a broader progressive majority" that can "overcome the resistance of the elites".

Housing has not been the only issue causing problems for Sánchez's leadership in recent months, with his party having been caught up in numerous corruption scandals and facing pressure on other cost-of-living issues and immigration.

"We have made mistakes and have not achieved everything we had set out to do," Sánchez said, acknowledging there were still "a lot of problems to solve, particularly in the areas of inequality, of public services and access to housing".

Sánchez's left-wing coalition government is made up of his ruling Socialist party and junior partner the Sumar alliance, and does not have a majority in parliament.

Spain was not due to hold a general election until the summer of 2027 at the latest.

Sánchez has been prime minister since June 2018. His Socialist party finished second in the last election, in 2023.

Although the conservative People's Party won the most seats, it fell short of a majority.

Sánchez remained in power after striking agreements with left-wing parties and securing support from Catalan and Basque nationalist and pro-independence groups.

Most opinion polls suggest the conservatives are likely to emerge as the largest party in the next election. However, they would be expected to need the support of the hard-right Vox party to form a government.

Speaking after Monday's announcement, the leader of the People's Party, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said: "At last, Spaniards will be able to decide".

The opposition leader said it would not be "just another election", but a chance for voters to choose between "decline or change, lies or change, incompetence or change, division or change, corruption or change".

On Saturday, tens of thousands of people took to the streets in cities including Madrid, Valencia and Barcelona, calling for greater protections for tenants.

Maricarmen Abascal, 87, became a symbol of Spain's housing crisis when she was forcibly evicted from her Madrid home on 23 September.

A legal glitch allowed her landlord to raise her rent from €500 (£428; $572) to €2,650. It was later lowered to €1,650 - still €300 more than her monthly pension.

She was removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years, and was later admitted to hospital.

Her lawyer has since said she will be able to return to her home , but the incident has prompted widespread anger over housing.

The left-wing coalition government responded with two decree laws in an effort to defuse the protests.

The first included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".

The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the tenants' organisation Sindicato de Inquilinas.

The political right argued the government's attempt to intervene in the housing market would have led to fewer homes being rented and would have raised prices further.

Juan Bravo of the People's Party said last week "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

Sánchez's leadership has been marred by numerous corruption scandals in recent months.

In April, his wife Begoña Gómez was charged with corruption after a two-year criminal investigation.

She is accused of using her relationship to advance her private career - allegations she denies, and which have been dismissed by Sánchez as a right-wing attempt to undermine his coalition.

In May, police raided the Socialist party's headquarters in Madrid as part of an investigation into allegations an operative was paid to carry out a misinformation campaign. The party has denied the allegations.

And in June, Sánchez's former transport minister, José Luis Ábalos, was jailed for 24 years after he was found guilty of being involved in a network that received kickbacks from the sale of face masks during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The Spanish prime minister also came under scrutiny for his handling of the Ceuta migration crisis over the summer, when tens of thousands of people entered the territory from Morocco without authorisation.

items.title: Apple and a Hacker's Future
items.summary: Article URL: https://stratechery.com/2026/apple-and-a-hackers-future/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49962857 Points: 132 # Comments: 119
items.content:
My computer got hacked, which is always embarrassing to admit, because it was my fault; the vulnerability that was exploited is detailed in this Ars Technica story :

Dutch officials have warned that a high-severity macOS vulnerability that allows attackers to execute malicious code is under active exploitation. “The NCSC has received a notification indicating that active abuse of this vulnerability has been observed on multiple systems on which port 5900 was accessible from the Internet,” the Netherlands National Cyber Security Centrum warned earlier this week. “In all these cases, root had been accessed on the affected system and a Monero crypto miner had been placed.”

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-65400, received a patch from Apple last week for macOS Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma. The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 7.1 out of 10, stems from a bug in the macOS screen sharing capability, which allows a remote party to view the screen and control the keyboard and mouse while a machine is turned on. A flaw in the “state management,” which keeps track of preceding events, user interactions, variables, and other system states, is the underlying cause.

A video of the exploit in action can be found here . Details of CVE-2026-65400 became public at last week’s Black Hat security conference. Apple said last week that CVE-2026-65400 “may” allow an attacker without credentials to gain access to a Mac. It’s unclear why Apple hedged, but softening language is common among most tech developers when disclosing vulnerabilities. Apple credited security firm Bynario for reporting the vulnerability.

The computer in question was my always-on Mac Mini that runs nothing but Claude and Codex; the first thing that makes this story interesting is that that was my saving grace.

I have discussed, in both Writing Things Down and in several episodes of Sharp Tech , Gecko, the agent that I have built for the people that work with me. It’s awesome, but purposely constrained in capability and in what it can access. My real agent is a dedicated Claude Code thread that writes down all of my ideas and tracks the status of the myriad of projects I’ve spun up over the last few months.

There are a few reasons why I use Claude for this functionality, even though I’m not a big fan of Claude-speak: Claude in its Code harness seems to handle wide-ranging discussions better than Codex, and it follows my instructions about writing things down in the way I want to more gracefully. Code also has a persistent monitoring tool that I utilize as an inbox to capture interactions with a status board I built to visually track everything I have written down, as well as interactions with a Telegram bot (OpenAI’s new Dots achieve some of this functionality , which has been sorely needed in ChatGPT/Codex).

Said monitoring tool stands down every 30 minutes, so my agent restarts it on a schedule; that is what triggered an URGENT notification from Claude:

Claude had more diagnostic information, unilaterally stopped executing all commands, and noted that my account could now run admin commands without a password, which it assumed was how the files were written; it then had a number of suggested next steps to address the problem. The one I ignored was its recommendation that I not invoke Claude anymore; in fact, I used Claude to root out the malware — we eventually found the exact four second period where it gained access — create a tool to watch for it in the future, and then wiped the Mac Mini.

All of this happened before I found the Ars Technica article detailing the vulnerability, and it was pretty remarkable. I understand that people are nervous about giving these agents access to one’s computer — as I noted, the Mac Mini in question has nothing on it except for Codex and Claude — but in this case you could make the case that I would have been in much more trouble had I not had an agent running persistently.

Apple doesn’t seem too happy about agents; last week the company’s developer site released a note entitled Updates to Full Disk Access in macOS ; I’m going to quote it in full:

We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.

Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.

To say that I’m nervous about what Apple’s solution will entail is a massive understatement. There is one aspect in which the Mac is the perfect agent host: Apple has, for decades, invested in a combination of scriptability, automation, and accessibility APIs (these are very often the same thing) that makes it remarkably well-suited to computer use. Then there is the fact that macOS is a certified Unix system; this means that agents — which are perfectly suited to the command line — have access to the entire universe of tooling built for Unix systems. And, of course, Mac hardware is amazing.

The problem is that for my particular use case — a headless, always-on Mac Mini that I primarily access from other computers and my phone through the ChatGPT and Claude apps — macOS is incredibly hostile. The biggest issue is GUI-only permission prompts that are invisible to software running on said computer, including agents.

These permission prompts are a part of a macOS subsystem called Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC), although Apple doesn’t seem to use this name anymore. There are a whole host of things on your Mac that are covered by TCC — the list only gets longer with every OS release — and you have to explicitly approve access to the covered items for every app that wants to access them. If you’ve been prompted for permission to use the Camera, or, much more annoyingly, access the Desktop or Downloads, you’ve encountered TCC.

This system is annoying but manageable on your primary Mac; it’s a disaster on a headless Mac running agents, for two reasons. First, agents write new programs all of the time, and in my case, those programs need access to devices on my network (SMB shares, for example, trigger a TCC warning). What I need is a permission layer for agents, not the programs they create; TCC is operating at the wrong level of abstraction.

Second, the TCC subsystem exposes its prompt in a protected space that no program can see; that means that programs silently fail and the agents don’t know why; what I have to do is remember that there is probably a permissions prompt on screen, log into the Mac Mini with screen-sharing software, and click OK.

There are in fact good reasons for this. The goal of the TCC subsystem is to protect you from malware accessing your computer nefariously; if the prompts were accessible by software running in userland then malware could work around it. Again, though, I am running a computer that is purpose-deployed for agents: for my use case TCC is nothing but a headache — one that indirectly led to my being hacked.

As noted by the NCSC, the vulnerability is being exploited when port 5900 is exposed to the Internet. When screen sharing is turned on, the macOS firewall opens the port. Routers and dedicated firewalls generally block the port unless configured to override that setting. Security practitioners generally advise Mac users to keep the port closed even when using screen sharing and to instead connect over a VPN or through SSH tunneling. The alternatives require actions that aren’t within the capabilities of most users.

The safest practice is to block screen sharing, enable it only when screen sharing is needed, and to turn the feature off once a session has ended. Screen sharing can be turned on or off by accessing System Settings > General > Sharing and toggling the switch for Screen Sharing. Of course, installing last week’s security update is also a must.

Obviously I should have — and will be — using a VPN going forward (the foundation of my entire approach to security is Tailscale ); what I will note, however, is that TCC basically leaves me no choice but to have screen sharing enabled if I want to actually use my Mac Mini in the way I want to use it. I use screen-sharing constantly — including from my phone — and almost every time it’s to click “OK” on a stupid prompt that I’ve long since stopped taking seriously; the reason I didn’t depend solely on Tailscale from the get go is that I wanted a secondary way to reach the Mac Mini (which should have been SSH tunneling; again, this is somewhat embarrassing and my fault).

items.title: Trump chooses top spy boss to run new AI taskforce
items.summary: The US president said his national intelligence chief will lead the group as worries over AI grow.
items.content:
US President Donald Trump has named the director of national intelligence as the head of a new taskforce on AI which, he said, will coordinate government engagement with consumers, companies and "religious organizations".

Jay Clayton will head a taskforce that has drawn criticism from the likes of Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren who has called for regulation of AI.

Trump has rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology despite a debate about the potential risks of AI and what it means for humanity.

Last week, the president and the heads of major AI firms signed a "morally binding" document, making them responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.

Trump - who is unilaterally attempting to rebrand AI as "super intelligence" - wrote on social media: "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies."

As well as Clayton, a former chair of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Andrew Ferguson, head of the Federal Trade Commission, will be on the taskforce along with Emil Michael, undersecretary of defense for research and engineering.

It will report directly to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

Trump has pushed back against any kind of slowdown on AI development. He said the US is leading the race ahead of China, adding: "And, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."

President Xi Jinping recently travelled to Washington for a state visit. Days later, Trump ruled out a joint venture between the US and China to develop AI.

"If we do that, we're going to be giving a lot of secrets that we have that they [China] would want to have, or anybody else," he said.

The announcement of the taskforce follows growing pressure from prominent figures in the industry, including executives of OpenAI and Anthropic, to tighten regulation of the technology.

Trump first announced the taskforce in September, prompting Warren to state: "Congress cannot meet the pressing threat of AI by just forming another committee or continuing to have drawn-out discussions about it."

She added: "Let's actually pass some meaningful regulations on AI to protect people."

In an interview published on 4 October, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the benefits of AI justify accepting some of its risks and argued that the technology should remain accessible to the public.

"The world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this ‌technology and people having the agency," Altman told Politico's technology-focused newsletter Decoded.

The company recently admitted that a rogue OpenAI agent hacked an Australian government website in June and accessed private data.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the agent "infiltrated" a statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare.

Despite the incident occuring in June, Albanese said the government only learned about the breach in August. He said there will be "legal consequences".

OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon is due to appear as part of an AI inquiry in Australia on Tuesday.

Over the weekend, a former leader in OpenAI's safety systems team wrote in an article for the Atlantic magazine that he had left the firm because its culture was "broken".

"As [OpenAI] sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed," wrote David Robinson, who was involved in safety and transparency reporting.

Last month, the ChatGPT-maker pulled the release of its latest AI model due to safety concerns.

Trump has largely left it to AI companies to regulate themselves.

A pact signed on 29 September included the signatures of executives from top tech firms like OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and Google.

On the same day, the president signed an executive order instructing US government departments and agencies to start using the terms "SI" and "Super Intelligence" and should no longer acknowledge the use of the term artificial intelligence.

SI will take the place of AI in "official correspondence", websites, reports and other forms of communication, the order said.

Some experts have questioned the logic of the rebranding, arguing that the use of "super intelligence" could cause confusion as it refers to more advanced systems.

Some top tech leaders have already started to use the new name, including multi-billionaire Elon Musk, who said on social media on Sunday that he will rename his firm's AI platform SpaceXAI as SpaceXSI.

Trump's AI rebrand causes 'unprecedented' demand for Slovenian website names

items.title: Trump vuole governare la “Super Intelligence”: nasce una task force federale
items.summary: Dopo aver ribattezzato l’IA “Super Intelligence”, Trump ha creato una task force federale che per ora ha 120 giorni per definire rischi e priorità ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Donald Trump ha annunciato la nascita della Super Intelligence Force (SIF), una task force federale che avrà l’incario di coordinare l'azione del governo statunitense sulla super intelligenza , il nome con cui l’amministrazione Trump ha scelto di indicare l'intelligenza artificiale. La notizia è arrivata domenica con un post su Truth, con la anche il nome che guiderà il gruppo: il direttore dell'intelligence nazionale Jay Clayton.

Trump ha presentato la struttura come il seguito dell'accordo con le grandi aziende tecnologiche siglato alla Casa Bianca, dove, scrive, queste avrebbero confermato le proprie responsabilità verso gli americani.

La SIF dovrà garantire che gli Stati Uniti restino al comando in una tecnologia che "molti dicono" più grande della rivoluzione industriale e di internet, e coordinare i rapporti del governo con interlocutori che vanno dai consumatori alle organizzazioni religiose, dai gestori di infrastrutture critiche alle aziende del settore .

Con Clayton il post cita il presidente della Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, il sottosegretario alla Guerra per la ricerca e l'ingegneria Emil Michael e il direttore dell'Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor, mentre il gruppo risponderà a Trump e alla capo di gabinetto Susie Wiles.

A settembre Trump aveva già promesso una AI Force, pur liquidando il dibattito sulla sicurezza come una bufala dei democratici della "sinistra radicale", e aveva firmato un ordine esecutivo per ribattezzare l'intelligenza artificiale "super intelligence", termine che sarà usato dalle agenzie federali ma che non pone obblighi agli enti terzi che avranno a che fare con esse.

Intorno all’”esistenza” della Super Intelligence in rete c’è anche una curiosità. La sigla SI coincide con il dominio nazionale della Slovenia , e il registro locale Register.si ha contato circa 4.800 nuove registrazioni .si nelle 24 ore precedenti al 23 settembre (giorno dell'annuncio) di cui più della metà delle prime risulta messa in vendita sul mercato secondario. Le registrazioni sono poi salite a circa 13.600 il primo ottobre.

Il consulente Adam Cochran, investitore di venture capital e analista indipendente, ha sostenuto che gli acquisti sarebbero iniziati prima dei discorsi di Trump, con centinaia di registrazioni a giugno e migliaia a luglio, fuori tendenza , ipotizzando il coinvolgimento di persone vicine al presidente e citando la cittadinanza slovena di Melania e Barron Trump. Ma secondo IBTimes non ci sono prove che la famiglia presidenziale possieda i domini o ne abbia incassato i proventi.

In ogni caso, tornando alla task force e alle indiscrezioni di stampa su di essa, la sua carta prevederebbe piani contro le minacce legate alla SI ma senza eccessi di regolamentazione che frenino innovazione e concorrenza. Il gruppo avrebbe 120 giorni per consegnare un rapporto su rischi e opportunità dell'IA.
